facts.statement: Paleontologist Dr. William Hammer first excavated Cryolophosaurus in 1991 from the Early Jurassic Hanson Formation in Antarctica.
facts.quote: Cryolophosaurus was first excavated from Antarctica's Early Jurassic, Pliensbachian aged Hanson Formation, formerly the upper Falla Formation, by paleontologist Dr. William Hammer in 1991.

facts.statement: Cryolophosaurus was the first carnivorous dinosaur and the first non-avian dinosaur officially named from Antarctica.
facts.quote: It was the first carnivorous dinosaur to be discovered in Antarctica, and the first non-avian dinosaur from the continent to be officially named.

facts.statement: Cryolophosaurus was the second dinosaur and the first theropod discovered in Antarctica.
facts.quote: Cryolophosaurus was the second dinosaur, and first theropod to be discovered in Antarctica.

facts.statement: Cryolophosaurus was formally named and described in 1994 by Hammer and Hickerson in the journal Science.
facts.quote: The specimens were formally named and described in 1994 by Hammer and Hickerson, in the journal Science.

facts.statement: Cryolophosaurus lived during the Early Jurassic Period, approximately 196 to 188 million years ago.
facts.quote: The sediments in which its fossils were found have been dated to about 196 to 188 million years ago, representing the Early Jurassic Period.

facts.statement: Subadult Cryolophosaurus was estimated to be 6 to 7 meters long and weigh between 350 and 465 kilograms.
facts.quote: It was one of the largest theropods of the Early Jurassic, with the subadult, being estimated to have reached 6 - 7 m long and weighed 350 - 465 kg.

facts.statement: Larger adult Cryolophosaurus are estimated to have reached a length of 8 meters.
facts.quote: The larger adults are estimated at 8 m (26 ft) in length.

facts.statement: Cryolophosaurus possessed a unique nasal crest that ran over the eyes, rose perpendicular to the skull, and fanned out.
facts.quote: It has a peculiar nasal crest that runs just over the eyes, where it rises perpendicular to the skull and fans out.

facts.statement: Studies suggest the distinctive crest of Cryolophosaurus was used for intra-species recognition.
facts.quote: Based on evidence from related species and studies of bone texture, it is thought that this bizarre crest was used for intra-species recognition.

facts.statement: The brain of Cryolophosaurus was more primitive compared to other theropods.
facts.quote: The brain of Cryolophosaurus was also more primitive than those of other theropods.

facts.statement: Cryolophosaurus is currently classified as a derived neotheropod closely related to Averostra.
facts.quote: Cryolophosaurus is currently considered to be a derived neotheropod, close to Averostra.

facts.statement: A 2020 study by Adam Marsh and Timothy Rowe classified Cryolophosaurus as a basal neotheropod.
facts.quote: However, a 2020 study conducted by Adam Marsh and Timothy Rowe found C. ellioti to be a basal neotheropod.

facts.statement: The classification of Cryolophosaurus remains debated due to its mix of primitive and advanced characteristics.
facts.quote: Classification of Cryolophosaurus is difficult because it has a mix of primitive and advanced characteristics.

facts.statement: New Cryolophosaurus material was unearthed in Antarctica in 2013, though its full description remains unpublished.
facts.quote: In 2013, new material of Cryolophosaurus was unearthed in Antarctica. The description of this material has not yet been published in a non-abstract form.

facts.statement: Researchers challenged the idea that the bizarre crest and armor of Cryolophosaurus were primarily for mating, fighting rivals, or intimidating predators.
facts.quote: Kevin Padian et al. (2004) challenged conventional hypotheses that the purpose of bizarre cranial structures and post-cranial armor in dinosaurs, was either for attracting mates, intimidating/fighting rivals in the group, or intimidating potential predators of other species.

facts.statement: Thomas R. Holtz Jr. suggested in 2010 that the crest of Cryolophosaurus was primarily used for intra-species recognition.
facts.quote: Thomas R. Holtz Jr. (2010) found that the bizarre crest of C. llioti was primarily for intra-species recognition, based on evidence from related species and studies of bone texture.

facts.statement: Thomas Rich and colleagues proposed that the crest was ineffective as a weapon but likely functioned as a display feature during social behaviors like mating.
facts.quote: According to Thomas Rich and his colleagues, the crest would have been ineffective as a weapon and may have possibly functioned as a display feature during certain types of social behavior such as mating.

facts.statement: In 2019, the species recognition function of the crest was disputed, while a socio-sexual display model was suggested.
facts.quote: In 2019, a species recognition function was disputed but a socio-sexual display structure model was suggested.

facts.statement: The discovery of long cervical ribs in the mouth of the type specimen led researchers to hypothesize that Cryolophosaurus was feeding on a prosauropod when it died.
facts.quote: When the type specimen was discovered, several long cervical ribs, of a supposed prosauropod dinosaur were found in the mouth of Cryolophosaurus, which led Hammer (1998) to conclude that it was feeding on the prosauropod when it died.

facts.statement: Hammer concluded that a post-canine tooth from a tritylodont was part of the stomach contents of the Cryolophosaurus specimen when it died.
facts.quote: Hammer also concluded that a post-canine tooth belonging to a tritylodont (an early mammal relative), found with the remains, was part of its stomach contents when it died.

facts.statement: Pathologies in some Cryolophosaurus bones provide evidence of scavenging behavior.
facts.quote: Some Cryolophosaurus bones have pathologies that show evidence of scavenging.

facts.statement: Rootless broken teeth from a juvenile Cryolophosaurus found nearby suggest they shed naturally while scavenging an adult carcass.
facts.quote: Broken teeth from a juvenile Cryolophosaurus were found nearby. These teeth have no roots and likely shed naturally while scavenging the adult Cryolophosaurus carcass.

facts.statement: Cryolophosaurus fossils were found about 650 km from the South Pole, which was approximately 1000 km farther north during the time the animal lived.
facts.quote: Cryolophosaurus was found about 650 km from the South Pole but, at the time it lived, this was about 1000 km or so farther north.

facts.statement: During the Early Jurassic, Antarctica had a cool temperate and humid climate with a temperature interval of 17–18 degrees Celsius, similar to modern southern Chile.
facts.quote: In the Early Jurassic, Antarctica was closer to the equator and the world was considerably warmer than today, but the climate was still cool temperate similar to that of modern southern Chile, and humid, with a temperature interval of 17–18 degrees.

facts.statement: Models suggest that coastal areas in Early Jurassic Antarctica probably never dropped much below freezing, though inland conditions were more extreme.
facts.quote: Models of Jurassic air flow indicate that coastal areas probably never dropped much below freezing, although more extreme conditions existed inland.

facts.statement: The genus Cryolophosaurus was described by Hammer & Hickerson in 1994.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Hammer & Hickerson, 1994

facts.statement: The species Cryolophosaurus ellioti was described by Hammer & Hickerson in 1994.
facts.quote: species_authority: Hammer & Hickerson, 1994

facts.statement: Cryolophosaurus ellioti is the only known species of the extinct Cryolophosaurus genus, a basal dilophosaurid theropod that lived during the Early Jurassic, approximately 186 to 182 million years ago, in what is now Antarctica.
facts.quote: Cryolophosaurus ellioti (gr. «Reptil de cresta congelada de David Elliot») es la única especie conocida del género extinto Cryolophosaurus de dinosaurio terópodo dilofosaurido basal, que vivió a principios del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente 186 a 182millones de años, en el Pliensbachiano, en lo que hoy es la Antártida.

facts.statement: Due to the strange crest on its forehead, Cryolophosaurus is popularly known as Elvisaurus, resembling the hairstyle of rock artist Elvis Presley.
facts.quote: Debido a la extraña cresta en su frente, es conocido popularmente como Elvisaurus, por lo parecido con el peinado del artista de rock Elvis Presley.

facts.statement: Cryolophosaurus is the first Antarctic dinosaur to receive a name, although the first one found was Antarctopelta.
facts.quote: Cryolophosaurus es el primer dinosaurio antártico en recibir nombre, aunque el primero en ser encontrado fue Antarctopelta.

facts.statement: Cryolophosaurus is the first theropod found in Antarctica and possibly one of the oldest known tetanurans.
facts.quote: Igualmente es el primer terópodo encontrado en la Antártida y posiblemente uno de los tetanuros más antiguos conocidos.

facts.statement: The brain of Cryolophosaurus was also more primitive than that of other theropods.
facts.quote: El cerebro de Cryolophosaurus también era más primitivo que los de otros terópodos.

facts.statement: Cryolophosaurus was excavated in Antarctica from Early Jurassic sediments in the Hanson Formation by paleontologist Dr. William Hammer in 1991.
facts.quote: Cryolophosaurus fue excavado en la Antártida en sedimentos del Jurásico Temprano, durante el Sinemuriano al Pliensbachiano en la Formación Hanson, anteriormente la formación Falla superior , por el paleontólogo Dr. William Hammer en 1991.

facts.statement: It was the first carnivorous dinosaur discovered in Antarctica and the first non-avian dinosaur from the continent to be officially named.
facts.quote: Fue el primer dinosaurio carnívoro en ser descubierto en la Antártida y el primer dinosaurio no aviar del continente nombrado oficialmente.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen FMNH PR1821 is the only fully described specimen of Cryolophosaurus.
facts.quote: El holotipo FMNH PR1821 es el único ejemplar completamente descrito de Cryolophosaurus.

facts.statement: New Cryolophosaurus material was discovered in Antarctica in 2013.
facts.quote: En 2013, se descubrió nuevo material de Cryolophosaurus en la Antártida.

facts.statement: Cryolophosaurus was a large, robust theropod and one of the largest of its time.
facts.quote: Cryolophosaurus era un terópodo grande y bien construido, uno de los más grandes de su tiempo.

facts.statement: William R. Hammer and William J. Hickerson estimated Cryolophosaurus length at 6 to 7 meters in 1999.
facts.quote: Se calculó que Cryolophosaurus tenía una longitud de 6 a 7metros por William R. Hammer y William J. Hickerson en 1999.

facts.statement: A 2007 study by Nathan Smith et al. revised the length estimate to 6.5 meters.
facts.quote: Un estudio de 2007 de Nathan Smith et al. revisó la longitud a 6,5metros.

facts.statement: The estimated weight of Cryolophosaurus is 465 kilograms.
facts.quote: Su peso estimado es de 465kilogramos.

facts.statement: Based on length and weight estimates, Cryolophosaurus is currently the largest known early Jurassic theropod.
facts.quote: Con base en estas estimaciones de longitud y peso, Cryolophosaurus es actualmente el terópodo más grande conocido del jurásico temprano.

facts.statement: The skull has an estimated length of 65 centimeters.
facts.quote: El cráneo tiene una longitud estimada de 65centímetros.

facts.statement: It possesses a peculiar nasal crest that runs just above the eyes, rising perpendicularly from the skull and expanding.
facts.quote: Tiene una peculiar cresta nasal que corre justo sobre los ojos, donde se eleva perpendicularmente al cráneo y se expande.

facts.statement: The crest is thin and deeply grooved, giving it the appearance of a Spanish comb.
facts.quote: Es delgado y muy surcado, dándole una apariencia de peine español.

facts.statement: Research found the fossil has an almost complete, undistorted cranial cavity sufficient to approximate the shape and size of the living brain.
facts.quote: El estudio encontró que el Cryolophosaurus fósil tiene una cavidad craneal casi completa, sin distorsión, lo suficientemente completa para dar una forma y tamaño aproximados del cerebro vivo.

facts.statement: Cryolophosaurus was originally found during the austral summer of 1990-91 by William Hammer and his team at Mount Kirkpatrick in the Beardmore Glacier region of the Transantarctic Mountains.
facts.quote: Cryolophosaurus fue originalmente hallado en el verano austral de 1990-91, por William Hammer y su equipo, en el monte Kirkpatrick, en la región glaciar Beardmore de la cordillera transantártica.

facts.statement: It was found in siliceous rocks of the Hanson Formation, formerly known as the Upper Fault Formation.
facts.quote: Fue hallado en rocas de sílice de la Formación Hanson, antiguamente la Formación Falla superior.

facts.statement: It is the first carnivorous dinosaur found in Antarctica and the first of any type to be named.
facts.quote: Es el primer dinosaurio carnívoro encontrado de la Antártida y el primero de cualquier tipo en ser nombrado.

facts.statement: It is dated to the Early Jurassic; originally described as the oldest tetanuran, but subsequent studies suggest it is more closely related to dilophosaurids.
facts.quote: Está datado en el Jurásico inferior, originalmente se lo describió como el más antiguo tetanuro, pero estudios subsecuentes han hallado que probablemente este más relacionado con los dilofosáurido.

facts.statement: Specimens were formally named and described in 1994 by Hammer and Hickerson in the journal Science.
facts.quote: Los especímenes fueron formalmente nombrados y descritos en 1994 por Hammer y Hickerson, en la revista Science.

facts.statement: The name Cryolophosaurus ellioti derives from Greek roots meaning 'cold', 'crest', and 'lizard'.
facts.quote: El nombre Cryolophosaurus ellioti deriva del griego κρυος (Cryo) que significa 'frío' o 'congelado', λοφος (lopho) 'cresta' y σαυρος (saurus) 'lagarto'.

facts.statement: Hammer and Hickerson named the species C. ellioti in honor of David Elliot, who made the initial discoveries.
facts.quote: Hammer y Hickerson nombraron a la especie C. ellioti por David Elliot, quien hiciera los descubrimientos iniciales.

facts.statement: Additional material was collected from the site during 2003.
facts.quote: Durante el 2003 se recolectó material adicional del sitio.

facts.statement: Cryolophosaurus is significant as the oldest known tetanuran on any continent, the only one from the Early Jurassic.
facts.quote: Cryolophosaurus es de gran significancia ya que es el tetanuro más antiguo conocido en cualquier continente, el único del Jurásico inferior.

facts.statement: It was originally thought to be a ceratosaurian or abelisaurid but was concluded to be the oldest known member of the Tetanurae group.
facts.quote: Originalmente se pensó que era un ceratosauriano o un abelisáurido, que muestran ejemplos de evolución convergente con los tetanuros pero finalmente llegó a la conclusión de que era en sí mismo el miembro más antiguo conocido de este último grupo.

facts.statement: However, new studies in 2007 demonstrated Cryolophosaurus was probably a ceratosaurian more closely related to Dilophosaurus and Dracovenator than to tetanurans.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, nuevos estudios en el 2007 demostraron al Cryolophosaurus era probablemente un ceratosaurido más emparentado con Dilophosaurus y Dracovenator que con los tetanuros.

facts.statement: In 2012, Matthew Carrano found Cryolophosaurus was a tetanuran related to Sinosaurus but not related to Dilophosaurus.
facts.quote: En 2012, Matthew Carrano encontró que Cryolophosaurus era un tetanuro, relacionado con Sinosaurus, pero sin relación con Dilophosaurus.

facts.statement: In 2015, Hendrickx et al. recovered Cryolophosaurus in a basal position within Tetanurae alongside Sinosaurus.
facts.quote: En 2015 Hendrickx et al. en su revisión de los terópos no avianos recupera a Cryolophosaurus en una posición basal de Tetanuare junto a Sinosaurus.

facts.statement: Thomas R. Holtz Jr. discovered in 2010 that the strange crest of Cryolophosaurus served primarily for intraspecific recognition based on related species evidence and bone texture studies.
facts.quote: Thomas R. Holtz Jr. en 2010 descubrió que la extraña cresta de Cryolophosaurus servía principalmente para el reconocimiento intraespecies, con base en la evidencia de especies relacionadas y estudios de textura ósea.

facts.statement: According to Thomas Rich and colleagues, the crest would have been ineffective as a weapon and possibly functioned as a visual signal during certain social behaviors like mating.
facts.quote: Según Thomas Rich y sus colegas, la cresta habría sido ineficaz como arma y posiblemente haya funcionado como una función de visualización durante ciertos tipos de comportamiento social, como el apareamiento.

facts.statement: Researchers initially found long cervical ribs of a supposed prosauropod dinosaur in the mouth of a Cryolophosaurus specimen, suggesting it ate the prosauropod when it died.
facts.quote: Cuando se descubrió el espécimen tipo, se encontraron varias costillas cervicales largas, de un supuesto dinosaurio prosaurópodo en la boca de Cryolophosaurus

facts.statement: Hammer suggested that the Cryolophosaurus individual might have drowned because the prosauropod ribs extended into the theropod's neck region.
facts.quote: Hammer notó además que debido a que las costillas se encontraron extendiéndose hasta la región del cuello del terópodo, este individuo puede haberse ahogado en estas costillas.

facts.statement: Smith et al. concluded that the cervical ribs belonged to the Cryolophosaurus specimen itself rather than to a separate prosauropod as Hammer proposed.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, Smith et al. llegó a la conclusión de que estos restos pertenecían al espécimen de Cryolophosaurus en sí, y no al "prosaurópodo" de Hammer.

facts.statement: Hammer concluded that a post-canine tooth belonging to a tritilodontid, an early mammal relative, found with the remains, was part of the stomach contents when the animal died.
facts.quote: Hammer también concluyó que un diente post-canino perteneciente a un tritilodontido, un pariente temprano de los mamífero, encontrado con los restos, era parte de su contenido estomacal cuando murió.

facts.statement: Pathologies found on some Cryolophosaurus bones show evidence of scavenging behavior.
facts.quote: Algunos huesos de Cryolophosaurus tienen patologías que muestran evidencia de carroñeros.

facts.statement: Broken teeth from at least two different theropods have been found near Cryolophosaurus fossils.
facts.quote: También se han encontrado dientes rotos de al menos dos terópodos diferentes cerca.

facts.statement: A possible pathology exists on the Cryolophosaurus ankle bone (astragalus), which was preserved with a small fibula splint located just above the ankle.
facts.quote: Otra posible patología se encuentra en el astrágalo, hueso del tobillo, de Cryolophosaurus. Este hueso se conservó con una pequeña férula del peroné ubicada justo arriba del tobillo.

facts.statement: Cryolophosaurus lived approximately 194 to 188 million years ago during the Sinemurian to Pliensbachian stages of the Early Jurassic.
facts.quote: Se descubrió en limolita "tufácea" depositada en la etapa Sinemuriense al Pliensbachiense del Jurásico temprano, hace aproximadamente 194 a 188millones de años.

facts.statement: Cryolophosaurus fossils were found in the Hanson Formation, part of the Transantarctic Mountains' Victoria Group, located at an altitude of approximately 4000 meters.
facts.quote: Esta formación geológica es parte del Grupo Victoria de las montañas Transantárticas, que se encuentra aproximadamente a 4000m sobre el nivel del mar.

facts.statement: The high altitude of the fossil site supports the idea that Early Jurassic Antarctica had forests populated by a wide range of species, at least along the coast.
facts.quote: La gran altitud de este sitio apoya la idea de que la Antártida del jurásico temprano tenía bosques poblados por una amplia gama de especies, al menos a lo largo de la costa.

facts.statement: Cryolophosaurus fossils were found about 650 km from the South Pole, but at the time the animal lived, this location was about 1000 km further north.
facts.quote: Cryolophosaurus se encontró a unos 650km del Polo Sur, pero que en el momento en que vivió, se encontraba a unos 1000km más al norte.

facts.statement: During the Early Jurassic, Antarctica was closer to the equator and the world was considerably warmer than today, though the climate remained temperate and cool.
facts.quote: En el jurásico temprano, la Antártida estaba más cerca del ecuador y el mundo era considerablemente más cálido que hoy, pero el clima todavía era templado fresco.

facts.statement: Jurassic air flow models indicate that coastal areas likely never dropped much below freezing, although more extreme conditions existed inland.
facts.quote: Los modelos de flujo de aire jurásico indican que las áreas costeras probablemente nunca cayeron mucho por debajo del punto de congelación, aunque las condiciones más extremas existían tierra adentro.

facts.statement: Cryolophosaurus belongs to the parent group Tetanurae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Tetanurae

facts.statement: Cryolophosaurus is classified in the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: The genus Cryolophosaurus was named by Hammer and Hickerson in 1994.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Cryolophosaurus (genus), Hammer and Hickerson 1994

facts.statement: The time range for Cryolophosaurus is recorded as 199.5 to 184.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Sinemurian to Pliensbachian (199.5 to 184.2 million years ago)
